tip.title: Use the two-minute rule for small tasks
tip.why: Quick tasks that linger on a to-do list create mental overhead. Knocking them out immediately frees working memory.
how: If a task takes less than two minutes, do it the moment it comes up.
For tasks that seem small but keep getting deferred, set a phone timer for two minutes and start.
tip.ask: What small tasks am I putting off right now?

markets.headline: Tech sell-off drags Nasdaq down 2% as AI bubble fears mount.
points: S&P Tech sector fell over 3%; CoreWeave's $50B debt pile spooked investors.
Energy led gains as oil climbed. Tesla rose after its Roadster reveal but couldn't lift the broader market.
Hotter CPI data pushed Treasury yields higher, adding pressure.

pick.name: CoreWeave
pick.what: CoreWeave provides GPU cloud infrastructure purpose-built for AI workloads.
pick.why: Dropped nearly 12% today on debt concerns — worth watching whether the sell-off is overdone. An idea to research, not a recommendation.
pick.risk: Roughly $50 billion in debt. If AI spending cools, servicing that load gets very hard.

btc.summary: Cowen's July memo projects a Q4 2026 Bitcoin bottom near $44,000, citing midterm-year seasonality and declining ETF holdings. MVRV Z-Score at 0.395 — wants it below zero for a durable bottom.

news.title: Tesla unveils flying Roadster with SpaceX cold-gas thrusters
news.blurb: Musk showed the Roadster performing jumps, rolls, and a controlled landing at SpaceX's McGregor facility. Compressed air thrusters enable brief flight and hovering.
news.ask: How practical are cold-gas thrusters in a consumer vehicle?

news.title: AI bubble fears mount as CoreWeave debt hits $50 billion
news.blurb: The Nasdaq sank 2.14% as investors questioned whether AI revenue can justify massive infrastructure spending. CoreWeave, with ~$50B in debt, fell nearly 12%.
news.ask: Is the AI infrastructure buildout outpacing actual demand?

different.title: There's a high-pitched hum that only young people can hear
different.blurb: The 'Mosquito' device emits a 17.4 kHz tone audible to most people under 25 but inaudible to most adults over 30, due to age-related hearing loss called presbycusis. It was originally designed to deter loitering teenagers — but teens repurposed the frequency as a ringtone teachers can't hear.
different.ask: At what age does hearing loss at 17 kHz typically become noticeable?
